templatesPage.cssHint: The literal content of a CSS file, applied while this template is selected. Redefining the same custom properties light/dark use — --color-bg, --color-surface, --color-text, --color-text-muted, --color-border, --color-accent, --color-danger, --color-danger-bg, plus color-scheme — is enough to reskin the whole app consistently, e.g.: :root { --color-bg: #fdf6e3; --color-text: #073642; color-scheme: light; }. Anything else a stylesheet can do is fair game too. Upload a .css file below — downloading light or dark's CSS above is a good starting point to edit and re-upload.

oidcSettings.intro: Let users log in via an external OpenID Connect identity provider (e.g. Pocket ID) in addition to the password form — any standards-compliant provider works, following its own discovery document rather than anything provider-specific.
oidcSettings.issuerHint: The provider's base URL, without a trailing slash — its OpenID discovery document is expected at "<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration".
oidcSettings.clientSecretHint: Leave blank to keep the current secret.
oidcSettings.autoProvision: Automatically create an account on first login
oidcSettings.autoProvisionHint: When disabled (default), only an email address an admin already created an account for can log in via OIDC. When enabled, a first-time login creates a new account at the level below.
oidcSettings.levelClaimHint: An account's name and level are also kept in sync with the provider on every login, independently of the setting above: the name comes from a "medinv_name" custom claim if present, otherwise from the standard "name" claim; the level comes from a "medinv_level" custom claim with the value "guest", "user", or "admin" — admin included. In Pocket ID, add a custom claim with the exact key you need to a user or group under Admin → Users/User Groups → Custom Claims. Any of these claims being absent leaves the corresponding field untouched.
